Commit message:
honor ChunkTransferTimeout in the gRPC Writer (#20634)

### Summary

Implements gRPC write stall detection for `Writer.ChunkTransferTimeout`,
covering both resumable and appendable uploads. A watchdog in
`gRPCWriter.writeLoop` cancels the attempt and returns
`stallTimeoutError` if GCS does not acknowledge outstanding data within
the timeout. The upload then resumes through the normal retry path.

### Behavior

- **Stage 1:** `StartResumableWrite`, `QueryWriteStatus`, the appendable
takeover handshake, and the `BidiWriteObject` stream open share one
timeout.
- **Data transfer:** the timer runs only while a flush or the final
request is waiting on GC

Commit message:
type the external redirect guard (#33887)

`externalRedirect()` passed its guard to `canActivate` as an inline
arrow function. `canActivate` accepts `CanActivateFn` as well as the
deprecated class-based guards, typed as `ProviderToken<any>`. Any
function also matches `ProviderToken<any>`, so TypeScript didn't check
the inline guard against `CanActivateFn`. For example, a guard returning
a number would still compile.

This declares the guard as a `CanActivateFn` before passing it to
`canActivate`, so its return value is type checked. The behavior is
unchanged. A comment explains why the type is needed, so it isn't
inlined again later.

The release job authenticates to npm through OIDC: it gets `id-token: write` and no
`npm-token`, and `actions/setup-node` no longer takes `registry-url`, whose placeholder
`_authToken` in `.npmrc` would shadow the OIDC flow. pnpm 12 exchanges the token itself,
and the npm of Node.js 26 from `.tool-versions` is newer than the 11.5.1 that trusted
publishing needs. The release job lists `contents: write` too, since a job with
permissions gets no others.

Commit message:
explain that `create index concurrently` migrations need `allOrNothing: false` (#8461)

A migration with `isTransactional(): false` runs its queries without the
master transaction, so they go to another pooled connection. With the
default `allOrNothing: true`, earlier migrations in the same run are not
committed yet, so a `create index concurrently` can't see a table they
created and hangs on a table they altered.

This adds a note next to `isTransactional()` in the migrations guide
(current docs and the 7.2 snapshot): set `allOrNothing: false` as well,
keep in mind that a failed run then leaves the earlier migrations

Commit message:
add RetryBackoff spans for retry backoffs (#20715)

Adds OpenTelemetry tracing for the retry backoff sleeps in `run()` (HTTP
and gRPC transports).

For each backoff the client records a `RetryBackoff` child span of the
operation span, covering the sleep. The span is recorded once the sleep
ends, with its start time set to when the sleep began
(`trace.WithTimestamp`), so it is not visible while the backoff is still
in progress — a deliberate trade-off that keeps the hot path free of
span bookkeeping when the operation span is not recording.

pacquet changeset.

The range constrains nothing users see: the published `pnpm` manifest

Commit message:
do not treat outputs named class or style as styling inputs

When a directive had an output whose public name is `class` or `style`,
the node was flagged as having a directive input with that name. The
template's `[class]` or `[style]` binding was then sent to directive
inputs instead of the element, found none, and its value was silently
dropped. Interpolated `class`/`style` attributes and host directives
that expose such an output were affected as well.

#14414 enabled the DirectPath to CloudPath fallback by default for
clients that enable DirectPath.

The fallback connection pool sends each request to the next channel in
round-robin order, so the requests of a read-write transaction do not
stay on the same channel. With DirectPath, each channel is connected to
a single Spanner frontend, so most requests of a read-write transaction
are forwarded to the transaction owner. This happens for every
transaction, not only after a fallback has occurred.

Commit message:
add experimental.WithGRPCKeepalive for gRPC clients (#20685)

## Motivation

`grpc-go` disables HTTP/2 keepalive pings by default. When a GCS
frontend task/host dies ungracefully (no TCP `FIN`/`RST`), an in-flight
`ReadObject` stream hangs until the kernel's TCP retransmission limit
expires — ~925 s with the default `net.ipv4.tcp_retries2=15` — and
**indefinitely** if the dead peer's host still answers bare TCP
keepalive ACKs (no kernel timer fires). Application‑layer PINGs are the
only client‑side mechanism that detects this case; they close the
connection within ~`Time+Timeout` so the client's retry logic can fail
over.

Commit message:
keep root tsconfig references to non-project tsconfig files (#37266)

## Current Behavior

When the root `tsconfig.json` references need rewriting (a project
reference is missing, stale, or duplicated), `@nx/js:typescript-sync`
keeps only the existing references whose `<ref>/tsconfig.json` has
`composite: true`.

A reference that names a tsconfig **file** rather than a directory, such
as a root-level `./tsconfig.workspace.json` that type-checks workspace

Commit message:
incremental cycle check for `avoidRedundantChunkLoads` (#11320)

`optimize_dynamic_entry_bits` rebuilt the whole chunk graph to check each fold for a cycle, so its cost grew quadratically with the number of atoms. `ReducedChunkGraph` now builds the graph once and updates it with each move. Every edge a move adds starts or ends at the chunk that receives the atom, so while the graph is acyclic, one search from that chunk decides the move. A graph that already has a cycle gets a full check only for a move out of its single multi-chunk strongly connected component. The output is byte-identical to `main`.

closes #11262

Commit message:
stop scanning the whole template for every expression (#18738)

Parsing a 90 KB component drops from 460 ms to 35 ms; typical components
parse ~30% faster.

`read_pattern` blanked out the entire template before the pattern with
`replace(/[^\n]/g, ' ')` to keep positions aligned, and
`acorn.parseExpressionAt` re-counted lines from the top of the file on
every call. Acorn never looks before `pos`, so the real template can be
the prefix, and acorn 8.18's `startLocation` takes the line we already
have from the locator.

The blanking also had `loc.column` off by one for every node inside a
destructured pattern (noted in #18087), hence the snapshot updates.

range and registry, and it matches only entries locked from that registry.

Commit message:
reject a commit PostgreSQL answered with ROLLBACK (#8499)

PostgreSQL doesn't raise when `COMMIT` runs in an aborted transaction
(e.g. after a caught unique violation). It answers with the command tag
`ROLLBACK`, and Kysely drops the tag, so `em.transactional()` and
`em.commit()` resolved even though every write was discarded. This still
happens with kysely 0.29.7.

The pool now uses a `pg.Client` subclass that rejects a `commit`
answered with `ROLLBACK`. Kysely then treats it like any other failed
commit (a deferred constraint violation, say), and the existing rollback
releases the connection.

Commit message:
reduce instructions in SIMD byte searches (#28423)

Perf optimization to byte searches, following on from #28387.

In the AVX2 version, the order of needles in needles arrays affects the
generated instructions. If two bytes which only differ in a single bit
are paired together, LLVM can check for those 2 bytes in 2 operations
instead of 3.

e.g. `<` and `>`:

- Separated: `(v == 0x3C) | (v == 0x3E)`  - 2 compares + 1 OR
- Paired: `(v & 0xFD) == 0x3C`  - 1 AND + 1 compare

(note the stack up to #28422 already did some refactoring after #28387)

update BufferPool Get/TryGet semantics (#20647)

Updates the experimental BufferPool interface (added in #20513 and
#20522) to match the revised design:

- `Get(maxSize)` is non-blocking and always returns a buffer regardless
of pool constraints (error only on allocation failure). It no longer
takes a context. Callers use it for the first buffer of each upload to
guarantee progress and avoid deadlocks.
- `TryGet(maxSize)` now returns `([]byte, bool, error)`: `false` when a
buffer cannot be provided within the pool's constraints, error only on
allocation failure.

update release fixture configuration atomically (#37598)

## Current Behavior

The independent-projects release fixture rewrites `nx.json` in place.
The daemon can read the file during that write and see an empty file or
a mix of old and new fields.

## Expected Behavior

Each update replaces `nx.json` with a complete file. Readers that
already opened the file retain the old contents. Later readers see the
new contents.

## Related Issue(s)

The configuration-read failure in the [October 17 nightly
run](https://github.com/nrwl/nx/actions/runs/39005012684) is consistent
with this race. Its cause in that run has not been confirmed.
